title: Multiply Strings
statement: Two non-negative integers are given as strings `num1` and `num2`. Return their product as a string — without converting the whole strings to integers.
idea: Multiply the way it is done on paper: every digit of `num1` times every digit of `num2`.

Where does each small product go? Digit `i` of `num1` times digit `j` of `num2` contributes to position **`i + j + 1`** of the result, and its carry to position **`i + j`**. (An m-digit number times an n-digit number has at most m + n digits.)
Working from the right, add each product to what is already in its cell, keep the last digit there and push the carry one cell to the left.

complexity.timeWhy: Every pair of digits is multiplied once.

steps.text: Our example: **`num1 = "23", num2 = "45"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
A 2-digit number times a 2-digit number has at most 4 digits, so `result` gets 4 cells. The product of digit i and digit j belongs in cell **i + j + 1**; its carry goes to cell **i + j**.
3 × 5 = 15. Add what is already in cell 3: 15. Keep its last digit **5** in cell 3 and carry **1** into cell 2.
3 × 4 = 12. Add what is already in cell 2: 13. Keep its last digit **3** in cell 2 and carry **1** into cell 1.
2 × 5 = 10. Add what is already in cell 2: 13. Keep its last digit **3** in cell 2 and carry **1** into cell 1.
2 × 4 = 8. Add what is already in cell 1: 10. Keep its last digit **0** in cell 1 and carry **1** into cell 0.
Join the cells into a string and strip leading zeros: **1035**.
